attribution.note: Marcus's own bullet in his own post, endorsed.

semantics.note: A compound claim. 'Sora went nowhere' is a firm observation. 'Veo2 is probably better' is hedged with 'probably', so under policy it is not scored. Only the first clause can be adjudicated.

contract.note: The contract scores the hedged 'probably better' clause and uses it to produce a mixed outcome, which policy forbids. Its reading of 'went nowhere' as no meaningful traction is fair and ordinary, so the firm clause is scored on that reading alone.

evidence.note: a16z/Similarweb, January 2025: Sora debuted at #23 among AI-first consumer websites. That is meaningful early traction inside the target period, though it ranked behind Hailuo and Kling and says nothing about retention.
Artificial Analysis arena, Feb 25 2025: Veo 2 ranked above Sora. This bears only on the hedged comparison, which is not scored.

reviews.rationale: The only scorable part is 'Sora went nowhere'. Within a month of release, Sora entered the top 25 consumer AI websites by visits (e1), which is meaningful traction under the contract's fair reading. Arena results favouring Veo 2 bear only on the hedged 'probably better' clause, which is not scored. Ranking behind two Chinese rivals does not amount to going nowhere.

attribution.note: Marcus's own bullet in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition captures the cumulative claim that many top people had left OpenAI. Dropping the named examples does not change what is committed.

contract.note: The definition of 'top people', the cumulative window, and the exclusion of sabbaticals are fair, ordinary readings.

evidence.note: Observer, Sept 2024, documents 2024 departures including Karpathy, Sutskever, Schulman, Murati, McGrew and Zoph, notes Amodei as a former employee, and says only two of the eleven founders remained active.

reviews.rationale: Contemporaneous reporting confirms that the named people left and that other senior figures (McGrew, Zoph, Leike) left before March 2025. That is a substantial group of senior departures, not isolated cases. Brockman's sabbatical is correctly excluded.

attribution.note: Marcus's own bullet in his own post.

semantics.note: Faithful wording. In context Marcus has just acknowledged 'tons of (mostly unpaid) users' and next says OpenAI is losing money per prompt, so 'clear business model' refers to a viable, profitable model.

contract.note: The contract counts any payment mechanism with paying users as a 'clear business model'. That stretches the claim against the speaker: he had already conceded the user base, and the surrounding bullets concern profitability. An informed reader would take it to mean a sustainable, profitable model.

evidence.note: 400M weekly users is a company figure relayed by the COO. It shows adoption, which the speaker does not dispute.
2M paying enterprise users, also a company disclosure. It shows a revenue mechanism but not whether the business model is viable or profitable.
The 2023 launch of ChatGPT Plus pricing predates the target period.

reviews.rationale: Under a fair reading, the claim is about whether OpenAI had a profitable, sustainable model for its killer app. The packet shows adoption and paying users but no profitability or unit-economics evidence, as its own stated gaps admit. The contract's subscription-exists reading is unfair, so the claim cannot be scored as contradicted on it.

attribution.note: Marcus's own bullet in his own post.

semantics.note: A cumulative observation that no one had reached AGI by scaling as of the post date. The scope 'them or anyone else' is preserved.

contract.note: Reading AGI as broadly human-level general intelligence is the ordinary meaning, and it is neither stretched for nor against the speaker.

evidence.note: ARC Prize, Dec 2024, an independent evaluator, states that o3 is not AGI and still fails some easy tasks.
International AI Safety Report, Jan 2025: a scientific synthesis describing uneven capabilities and failures on simple reasoning tasks.
The 2023 Sparks paper calls GPT-4 an early, incomplete AGI. By its own qualification, that does not establish human-level AGI.

reviews.rationale: Independent evaluations up to early 2025 rejected AGI status for the leading scaled systems and documented major gaps in generalisation. The only counterpoint, the Sparks paper, describes GPT-4 explicitly as incomplete AGI. No independently established counterexample exists by March 1, 2025.
